name: Side arm raise, left arm
setup: Face the camera about two metres back so it sees your hips and hands.
cues: Let your arm float up as if it’s resting on water.
Notice the moment your arm starts to feel heavy.
Keep your shoulder soft and away from your ear.
Lower it as slowly as you raised it.

name: Side arm raise, right arm
setup: Face the camera about two metres back so it sees your hips and hands.
cues: Let your arm float up as if it’s resting on water.
Feel your shoulder blade glide as the arm rises.
Breathe out as the arm comes down.
Lower it as slowly as you raised it.

name: Standing side bend
setup: Face the camera, feet hip-width apart, arms by your sides. Slide one hand down the outside of your leg until you feel a stretch along your side, then rise back up. Switch sides each time, like the figure.
cues: Slide your hand down your leg like honey dripping.
Feel the long side of your body open.
Rise back to standing just as slowly.
Keep your hips still. Only your upper body leans.

name: Slow squat, side-on
setup: Stand side-on to the camera, either side works, so it sees your whole body from head to feet.
cues: Sit back as if a chair is very far away.
Feel your weight spread across your whole foot.
Rise like you’re being lifted by a thread.
No rush at the bottom. Pause there if you like.

name: Both arms float overhead
setup: Face the camera about two metres back so it sees your hips and hands. Raise both arms out to the sides together.
cues: Breathe in as your arms float up.
Let your arms feel wide, like wings.
Keep your neck long and your shoulders low.
Breathe out slowly as your arms drift down.

name: Forward arm raise, side-on
setup: Stand side-on to the camera and raise the arm nearest to it, straight out in front of you. The camera needs to see your hip, shoulder and hand.
cues: Reach forward as if you’re offering something.
Let your arm rise towards the ceiling, only as far as feels easy.
Keep your ribs soft. Don’t lean back.
Let the arm sink down slowly, like a feather.

name: Slow knee lift, side-on
setup: Stand side-on to the camera and lift the knee nearest to it. Rest a hand on a chair or wall if you want to.
cues: Let your knee drift up as if a string is pulling it.
Stay tall through the standing leg.
Lift only as high as your hip likes.
Lower your foot to the floor without a sound.

name: Standing heel to seat, side-on
setup: Stand side-on to the camera with a hand on a chair or wall. Bend the knee nearest to the camera to bring that heel towards your seat.
cues: Let your heel float back towards your seat.
Keep your knees side by side.
Feel the front of your thigh lengthen.
Let your foot come down gently, like it’s landing on grass.

name: Standing roll-down, side-on
setup: Stand side-on to the camera, knees soft. Let your chin drop and roll down one vertebra at a time, then roll back up. The camera needs to see your shoulders, hips and knees.
cues: Let your head be heavy and lead the way down.
Peel your spine down one bone at a time.
Keep your knees soft. Your hands just hang.
Stack yourself back up, head last.

name: Slow lunge, side-on
setup: Stand side-on to the camera with one foot a big step in front of the other. Lower straight down, then rise back up. The camera needs to see you from head to feet.
cues: Sink straight down, like an elevator.
Keep your front knee over your ankle.
Only go as low as feels steady.
Rise up slowly, pressing through both feet.

name: Rock back to child’s pose
setup: Put the camera low and side-on to you. Kneel on all fours with your hands under your shoulders. Rock your hips back towards your heels, then forward again.
cues: Let your hips drift back towards your heels.
Keep your hands where they are and let your arms lengthen.
Breathe into your back as it rounds.
Come forward slowly, like the tide coming in.

name: Slow bridge, lying down
setup: Put the camera low and side-on to you. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, arms by your sides. Lift your hips, then lower them back down.
cues: Press gently through your feet and let your hips rise.
Peel your back off the floor one bone at a time.
Lift only until your body is a long line.
Lower your spine back down slowly, as if setting down something precious.
